_comment: Source content for the PDFs Chia sends students. Each top-level key is a 'kind'; each nested key under it is a 'subject'. To add a new PDF: add an entry here, ensure lib/pdf/index.ts has a generator for the kind, then preview at /admin/pdfs.

ser.title: SER
ser.subtitle: to be (permanent: identity, origin, time, profession)

estar.title: ESTAR
estar.subtitle: to be (temporary: location, mood, ongoing state)

tener.title: TENER
tener.subtitle: to have — used for possession, age, sensations (tengo hambre, tengo años)

dating.title: Dating in Spanish
dating.subtitle: Phrases that actually work — from first hello to first kiss.

sections.heading: Showing interest
rows: You have an incredible look in your eyes.

sections.heading: Asking them out
rows: Want to grab a drink another day?
Want to meet up this week?

sections.heading: Getting closer
rows: I feel really good with you.
Want to come home with me?

pickup_lines.title: Piropos clásicos
pickup_lines.subtitle: Spanish pickup lines. Use with confidence and a smile — half of them are intentionally cheesy.

sections.heading: Cheesy classics
rows: ¿Tienes mapa? Es que me he perdido en tus ojos.
Do you have a map? I got lost in your eyes.
Did it hurt when you fell from heaven?
Si la belleza fuera delito, ya estarías en la cárcel.
If beauty were a crime, you'd already be in jail.
¿Crees en el amor a primera vista o tengo que pasar otra vez?
Believe in love at first sight, or do I need to walk by again?

sections.heading: Flirty + cheeky
rows: Me gustaría ser bizco para mirarte con los dos ojos.
I wish I were cross-eyed so I could look at you with both eyes at once.
Tantas curvas, y yo sin frenos.
So many curves, and me with no brakes.
¿Tu padre es ladrón? Porque robó las estrellas para ponerlas en tus ojos.
Is your dad a thief? He stole the stars and put them in your eyes.
Si fueras un libro, no te dejaría hasta el final.
If you were a book, I wouldn't put you down until the end.

sections.heading: More direct (use sparingly)
rows: Estoy perdido. ¿Puedes guiarme a tu corazón?
I'm lost. Can you guide me to your heart?
Se me olvidó tu nombre — ¿me lo dices con un beso?
I forgot your name — could you tell me with a kiss?
Si Cristóbal Colón te viera, diría: ¡tierra a la vista!
If Columbus saw you, he'd say: land ahoy!

dirty_jokes.title: Chistes verdes en español
dirty_jokes.subtitle: Spanish 'dirty' jokes — most are double-entendres rather than crude. Reading these in Spanish is great pronunciation practice; using them at dinner with new in-laws is at your own risk.

sections.heading: Plays on words
rows: —Doctor, no puedo hacer pis. —¿Cuántos años tiene? —98. —Ya ha hecho usted bastante.
—Doctor, I can't pee anymore. —How old are you? —98. —You've peed enough.
—Mamá, ¿cómo nací yo? —Te trajo la cigüeña. —¿Y mis hermanos? —También. —¡Qué activa la cigüeña!
—Mom, how was I born? —The stork brought you. —And my siblings? —Same. —Busy stork!
¿Qué hace una abeja en el gimnasio? Zum-ba.
What does a bee do at the gym? Zum-ba. (zumba = both the workout and 'buzz')

sections.heading: Wordplay with curse words (mild)
rows: Estoy hasta los cojones — y con las pelotas hinchadas.
I'm fed up — and my balls are swollen. (idiom + literal at once)
No tengo pelos en la lengua, ¡pero sí en otros sitios!
I don't have hair on my tongue (= I'm blunt) — but I do elsewhere!

sections.heading: Classic short ones
rows: —¿Cuál es el animal más viejo? —La cebra. Está en blanco y negro.
—What's the oldest animal? —The zebra. It's in black and white.
—¿Por qué los peces no van a la escuela? —Porque ya están en el escuelo. (banco)
—Why don't fish go to school? —They're already in 'el escuelo.' (banco = school of fish AND bank — wordplay)
How do you say 'tissue' in Chinese? 'Blow-your-nose.'
